Hi Elena -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can get you meaningful results quickly: 

Summary of needs (as discussed)
- Primary use case: long-form document summarization and extraction across multi-chapter PDFs and merged logs (~50-100k tokens).
- Key success metrics: summarization fidelity (ROUGE/Lexical overlap + factuality checks), end-to-end latency under 1s per 1k tokens for interactive workflows, and truncation behavior at >32k contexts.
- Constraints: PII redaction requirements, on-prem option for later phase.

What we recommend to evaluate model fit (next 2-3 weeks)
1) Run a targeted long-context eval using the sample docs you shared: we suggest the attached prompt set (acme-eval-prompt-set.csv) and the Redwood long-context benchmark (linked).
2) Models to test: 
   - redwood-rlhf-32k (baseline, high-fidelity summarization)
   - redwood-32k-quant (cost-optimized quantized variant)
   - open-llm-64k (to stress truncation; compare summarization drop-off)
3) Config notes: preserve KV cache on chunked inference, enable prefix caching for repeated sections, and run batch sizes of 4 for throughput tests.

We attached: acme-eval-prompt-set.csv (prompt templates & labeling guidelines) and a short benchmark write-up (redwood-long-context-benchmarks.pdf). Can you confirm the sample set we should use from your side (we saw the shared Drive link) and whether we can run the eval on Redwood hosted environment or if you prefer Dedicated/Private?

Proposed timeline
- This week: confirm prompt set and sample docs (you)
- Next week: Redwood runs initial evals and sends results + plots (we)
- Week after: 1-hour review call to go over regressions, recommended model, and cost/latency tradeoffs

Next steps for you
- Reply with which model variants you want prioritized (we recommend the three above), and confirm whether we should run on hosted infra or a Dedicated eval.

Thanks - looping in Vivek for the technical configuration and Rishi for pricing/contract implications.

Best,

Hi Elena / Marissa -

Thanks for the summary, Marissa. A few technical clarifications and recommendations so the eval exercise produces actionable signals: 

1) Context window strategy
- For documents in the 50-100k token range we recommend a hybrid approach: a 32k model with chunked sliding-window summarization + a retrieval-augmented step that passes only the most relevant segments to a 64k-capable model for final synthesis. This reduces cost while preserving fidelity.
- Truncation behavior: expect progressive degradation in attribution past the model's native window - our eval harness will track token-level retention for the last N sections and surface where hallucination/factuality drops.

2) Metrics & QA
- Quantitative: ROUGE-L, normalized BLEU, token retention (how many unique entities survive truncation), and latency per 1k tokens.
- Qualitative: crowd-annotated faithfulness checks + prompt-sensitivity analysis (we'll run the same prompt set with temperature sweeps).

3) Model recommendations (typical trade-offs)
- redwood-rlhf-32k: best fidelity, higher cost. Good for final summarization uses.
- redwood-32k-quant: ~2-3x cost savings, small drop in precision on extraction tasks.
- open-llm-64k: useful as stress test for truncation; watch for increased latency and more inconsistent factuality on dense tables.

4) Runtime config to capture truncation specifics
- Enable per-token logging (we'll anonymize PII) so you can see where the model starts dropping entities.
- Turn on prefix/KV caching to measure throughput gains when users re-query similar sections.

5) Privacy/compliance note
- If you want to keep data in your VPC for this eval, we can stand up a short-lived Private deployment for the run (takes ~3-5 business days). Otherwise hosted evals use encrypted data-in-transit and are isolated per account.

I attached a short benchmarks PDF that has past runs on our 32k/64k variants. I'll also prepare a sample eval harness config and share a Drive link by EOD.

--Vivek
